title: Walk behavior in the unary loop
statement: Let $C$ be a family of directed acyclic circuits, let $lm$ be a Boolean, let $n,i,B,V,U$ be natural numbers, and let $o$ be a Boolean oracle on the five query indices and bit strings. Suppose $V	ext{,}U\le B$. For every $d,W,k$ with $W+d=U$, $k\le i$, and $k+d+1\le B$, start the walk on the encoding of $1^n$ paired with the binary expansion of $i$, in state $uL$, with register values $(k,V,U,W)$ and no answer recorded. If $k\le i<k+d+1$, the walk halts with answer $lm$ or the $(i-k)$-th bit of the word consisting of $d$ ones followed by zero, and every earlier configuration has all register values at most $B$. If $k+d+1\le i$, the walk reaches a configuration with state $aN$, register values $(k+d+1,V,U,U)$, and no answer recorded; every configuration before reaching it has all register values at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $o$ is a Boolean oracle on five query indices and bit strings
